message:
Nathaniel, I wanted to check whether you’re available for a quick paperback-cover job.

• The cover needs 5 small fixes, limited to deleting a few words from my blurb and making the title font consistent across the front, spine, and back. Everything else is final, so no redesign is required.
• Please provide a layered .psd, a .pdf, and a .jpg.
• I need the completed files within 72 hours.

Would you be available? My budget is $90.

Best,
Marisol
Hello, Marisol.
Yes, I’m free to take this on.
Marisol, let’s go ahead with the project.
Shown here is a paperback book cover I completed recently.

Thanks for getting back to me so quickly, Nathaniel.

Five small fixes are needed, but this is not a redesign:
• The trimmed final paragraph of the blurb currently overlaps the barcode, so it only needs to be dropped in and reflowed.
• The front title uses a bold gold-gradient font, while the spine and back use a plainer one. Please match both of those to the front.

I’ll provide the images, templates, and the .psd. Would you be able to return a layered .psd, along with the .pdf and .jpg, within 72 hours?
Yes, that works for me, Marisol.

Thanks! I’ll send the job invitation and upload the information.

Best,
Marisol
Marisol, I appreciate the opportunity—thank you.
The editable files are what I’m waiting to receive.

For comparison, I’m including book 4 (The Glass Orchard) as a reference for the fonts currently used on book 7’s spine and back cover. I’d like the fonts to be uniform, so please let me know if anything is unclear.

Best,
Marisol
The upload failed for the .psd, so I’ll upload it again now.
As I review them now, I’ll let you know if any questions come up. Could you confirm, though, that your book has 420 page counts?

Yes—the book is 420 pages, and the Amazon print edition is also 420 pages. For print distribution, Draft2Digital uses Ingram, whose process added 8 pages to my book; I still don't know whether that affects the spine. Because I can't stop D2D from making the page count 428 instead of 420, I'm shortening the blurb. The issue is the bar code.
The difference is clear in the templates: D2D has a spine of 0.82 inches, while Amazon's is 0.90 inches.

Because the two platforms may not have the same specs, the safer approach is to create a separate cover for each one. I understand Amazon and Ingramspark: to allow for Ingram's 8 pages addition, we can prepare the first version at 420 and the second at 428. It's better this way.
Excellent idea.
The project is clear to me now, Marisol, and I will update you in 8 hours. Your message arrived just as I was about to leave my work desk.
Thanks, that’s excellent. Does our price agreement still stand?
Since we’ll now be working on both Amazon and Ingramspark, you can add $45 for the Ingramspark work. Ohhh—we haven’t discussed the price yet.
Marisol, what feedback do you have on that? Please let me know.

Of course. While I’m asking D2D whether its template generator has a bug, please start the blurb and font corrections. With 420–424 pages on Cream paper, the spine should be approximately 0.90" and exactly match my Amazon file. Instead, D2D keeps producing 0.82", even though I followed its instructions to resave Step 2 and download a fresh template. I definitely want the blurb and font fixed now, and I’ll update you soon about the spine.
Okay—we’re good to go, so we can begin with Amazon. The 8 pages addition from Ingram is not something I have encountered before.
That's quite an unpleasant surprise. :)
Until D2D responds, let's avoid any spine change and keep the cover at 420 pages / 0.90" spine. Thanks!
Okay.

This screenshot shows that the requested changes are complete. The spine-title font and back-cover font now match the font used for the title on the front. The chosen spine width is also in place, and the cover meets Amazon requirements overall.
Before I deliver all the files, can you update me on the second one?
D2D may use criteria different from Amazon. I'll independently confirm this from my end.
I'm happy with how it looks. Is there a way to download it and test it on D2D's platform?
The wait is ongoing: no news has arrived from D2D yet, which is very frustrating.
So that you can test it, I’ll send you the PDF file. Yes, sure.
thanks
Here it is—the file is 410MB. I'll be waiting for your results on D2D.

Hi Nathaniel,

While I wait for D2D, I’ll post on its social media to see whether that gets a faster response. Separately, there is an issue with your cover:

• Both the blurb edit and the title-font correction look good and were completed properly.
• The tagline at the top of the front cover ("DEATH AT THE LANTERN FESTIVAL") is appearing as garbled, corrupted text rather than the intended words.
• Font substitution or an encoding problem may be responsible, so please check which font that text box uses.
• For the new export, either embed the fonts or outline/convert them to curves. This will prevent the text from depending on local font availability and ensure that it renders correctly everywhere.
• Please correct the problem and resend the .pdf before the other files.

Thx
I'll investigate the issue right away. Okay.
Sorry about the earlier error; I've now corrected it.
Since it's launch day, I need to do social media first. Got it; I'll get back to you next Monday. Hopefully, D2D will have responded by then. Thkx.
Great, that sounds good to me.

With D2D still silent, I can't believe I haven't heard back yet. Let's pause this until next Thursday. In the meantime, I'll order something, though its cover specs may or may not be right. I'll give them three more days. Thanks for your patience. Best, Marisol
Understood, Marisol.
The issue still doesn't appear to be fixed, Nate. Please redo it and personally check the result before resending.
I'll test it once more.
It may be that I sent the previous file.
The file I send you will be the correct one.

I'm retesting now because the old/cached file may have been used by mistake.

D2D update: we still need 4 separate covers (Amazon + Ingram), while D2D's spine of 0.82" conflicts with Ingram's own formula, which gives 0.905". This remains unresolved and may take 96-120 hrs.

Until I confirm the correct number, do not build anything to 0.82". I'll follow up shortly.
To confirm, are you working directly with Five platforms, including Amazon, Ingramspark and D2D?
Are all five platforms going to carry your book?
It isn't three direct platforms: the direct channels are AMazon and D2D, while D2D uses Ingram's network for print.
Okay.

Nate, could we keep this job open for another four or five days? I can't verify the specification myself because I don't have an Ingram account, so I've asked D2D directly which paper-thickness factor they're using. It may simply be that Ingram's cream stock genuinely runs thinner than Amazon's, which could account for the spine difference. Unfortunately, D2D is slow to reply, so while I wait, I'll ask some author FB groups whether anyone knows. Very frustrating. The upside is that I now know to have 4 covers made; I didn't have this problem with book 1 :). In the meantime, can you confirm the page count, font, and other settings you used for the updated cover? Thanks!
That's fine with me, Marisol.
Once I resend the Amazon cover shortly, that part will be finished and only D2D will remain.
After downloading the most recently sent file, this is the screenshot I see on my end.
When I tried uploading your latest file to Amazon just now, it failed. I have no idea why; the error message itself is the only information provided.

According to my AI, font embedding could be the issue. Earlier in this project, we found a font that wasn't embedded or outlined correctly, which caused garbled text in another viewer. The fonts in the current file may likewise be incompletely embedded, and KDP's processor could be stricter about that than the preview tool I used.
All fonts show as embedded in the PDF font details—here they are.
Since the cause is still unclear, I'm stuck.
Since its size may be more than Amazon can process, I'll send you a newly exported pdf file.
Go ahead and send the smaller file. Although Amazon does allow for 900 MB, a bloated file can still make uploads more prone to timing out or failing midway through the transfer. thx.
Without changing the print quality, I've optimized the PDF file size so the upload should go more smoothly.
At last, the bigger file uploaded successfully. I’ll retain the smaller file as a backup.
Good—that result works for me.
The D2D cover is all that remains.
yep

Hi Nathaniel,
Please proceed with the D2D cover using the D2D template’s spine width of 0.82 inches. I’ll add $45 by modifying the job. Although D2D still hasn’t responded, I find it hard to believe there is a bug in its template; otherwise, many authors would be complaining.
Thanks,
Best,
Marisol
The D2D template is attached.
Got it, Marisol.
Optimized version
Two have a lower file size, although all four files are otherwise the same. Please upload this to D2D and give me feedback.
I'll start testing it now—thanks.
Please provide the final product in all three formats: PDF, .PSD, and .JPG.
Apologies, but could you resend the PDFs? I can’t tell now which file is for amazon at 420 pages and which one is for D2D at 428 pages. thkx
I’ve already sent the PDFs, but yes, sure—I can send them again. Should I include them with the deliveries once more?
yes please
Okay

Nathaniel, please send the files over. I’m ready to end the contract, but there’s another D2D issue: Amazon appears on its print setup page, and I can’t tell whether they’ll distribute there. If they distribute to Amazon, it would duplicate my listing, triple my commission, and could get me in trouble with Amazon. Until they reply, I still can’t publish through D2D. That problem is mine, not yours.
No problem. I’m currently preparing the files for delivery as a ZIP. Since the Amazon item is sorted, you can approve the fourth $90 payment. Only D2D remains.
